ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, AB is the diameter of the semicircle O, and point D is the midpoint of the arc AC. If $\angle BAC = 44^\circ$, then what is the value of $\angle DAC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $AB$ is the diameter of the semicircle $O$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$,\\
since $\angle BAC = 44^\circ$,\\
then $\angle B = 90^\circ - \angle BAC = 46^\circ$,\\
as quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in semicircle $O$,\\
then $\angle D = 180^\circ - \angle B = 134^\circ$,\\
given that point $D$ is the midpoint of arc $AC$,\\
it follows that $ \overset{\frown}{AD} = \overset{\frown}{DC}$,\\
thus $AD = DC$,\\
therefore $\angle DAC = \angle DCA = \frac{1}{2} (180^\circ - \angle D) = \boxed{23^\circ}$,

From the text, use AB as the diameter, D as midpoint of arc AC, and ∠BAC = 44°. Since AB is a diameter, ∠ACB = 90° by Thales' theorem, so in triangle ABC, ∠ABC = 90° - 44° = 46°. Also because D is the midpoint of arc AC, arc AD = arc DC, and the corresponding chords AD = DC, therefore triangle ADC is an isosceles triangle, ∠DAC = ∠DCA. Thus ∠DAC = (180° - 134°) / 2 = 23°.
